Who is Jeff?: Jeff is a Domestic Shorthair cat who lives in southern New Hampshire.
Can I meet Jeff?: If you're reading this, that means you've already met Jeff. I'm sure he's happy that you're here!
Okay, but can I actually meet Jeff?: No, sorry. Jeff is shy, lives indoors, and is not currently accepting visitors, interviews, or requests for his autograph.
Is \"Jefferson\" his real name?: Yes, Jefferson Elmer is his real government name. He arrived with the name "Jefferson" and, when questioned about it, gives us a narrowed gaze and refuses to answer.
Why is his middle name Elmer?: I gave him that name because he looks like he was assembled with glue. I assure you, however, that Jeff is (mostly) structurally sound.
How old is Jeff?: The shelter estimates that Jeff was born around 2018. He has yet to provide us with a birth certificate.
Does Jeff know about this website?: Yes, he has been informed. When I told him, he stared at me for several seconds and then left the room, which his representatives have described as "neither approval nor disapproval".
Did Jeff approve these pictures?: Jeff was given several opportunities to comment. He responded by biting the corner of the release form.
Why does Jeff look different in every pi: The photos were taken with different cameras, settings, lighting, and angles. There is also the possibility that Jeff uses similar-looking cats as stand-ins for public appearances.
Why are there exactly 150 pictures?: One hundred photos failed to capture the full range of Jeff's personality. However, 151 would have been excessive.
Will you add more pictures?: Probably not. The website has limited storage, and Jeff's complete photographic archive could threaten the structural integrity of GitHub.
Why did I see the same picture again?: The website avoids repeating pictures that have been displayed recently, but previously discovered ones can eventually return. Jeff believes that every photograph of him demands an encore.
Where is my progress saved?: Your discoveries and settings are stored locally in your browser. Clearing your browser data or using a different browser gives Jeff the opportunity to pretend that you have never met him.
Why are there \"Meet Jeff\" stickers?: Stickers were given to friends and family with instructions to place them alongside other stickers in designated public art spaces. If you found a sticker and arrived here, then the Jeff experiment has succeeded.
This sticker shouldn't be here. How can: Whoops... sorry about that. Carefully lift a corner with your fingernail or a plastic edge and peel slowly. If appropriate for the surface, gentle heat may help loosen the adhesive. If residue remains, use a surface-appropriate adhesive remover or isopropyl alcohol only after testing it in an inconspicuous area.
